name: United States v. Vaello Madero
summary: The Supreme Court held that Congress did not violate the Constitution by excluding Puerto Rico residents from Supplemental Security Income benefits, declining to overrule the Insular Cases framework.
significance: The Court's most recent engagement with the Insular Cases confirmed that Congress may treat territories differently from states in certain respects, which the government cites to argue that different environmental review standards in territories are constitutionally permissible.
